# OpenShell Dashboard Helm chart

<!-- Generated by helm-docs; edit README.md.gotmpl and values.yaml, then run `mise run helm:docs` -->

Deploys one stateless dashboard Deployment alongside an [OpenShell gateway](https://github.com/NVIDIA/OpenShell/tree/main/deploy/helm/openshell). Only the oauth2-proxy sidecar is exposed. The BFF binds `127.0.0.1:8080`; the Service and NetworkPolicy expose only proxy port 4180. The chart creates no gateway certificates, database, cluster RBAC, or certgen job.

## Install

Install the upstream gateway into the **same namespace**, release name `openshell` (or override `gateway.serviceName` / `gateway.url`). Set `server.oidc.issuer`, `server.oidc.audience`, `server.oidc.rolesClaim`, `server.oidc.adminRole`, and `server.oidc.caConfigMapName` there to the same values as `oidc.*` here. For OpenShift, layer `ci/values-openshift-scc.yaml` and `ci/values-route-edge.yaml`. Replace sample issuer and host before installing.

Create a confidential client `openshell-dashboard` at the same IdP with `https://<dashboard-host>/oauth2/callback` as its redirect URI. Its **access token** must have `aud` containing gateway `server.oidc.audience` (`openshell-cli` by default). Keycloak needs an audience mapper for this client; an ID token or oauth2-proxy's `--pass-authorization-header` is not a substitute. Provision the Secret outside Helm (the cookie secret must be a random 32-byte value):

```sh
kubectl -n openshell create secret generic openshell-dashboard-oidc \
  --from-literal=client-secret='<client secret>' \
  --from-literal=cookie-secret='<random cookie secret>'
helm upgrade --install openshell-dashboard ./deploy/helm/openshell-dashboard \
  -n openshell -f ./deploy/helm/openshell-dashboard/ci/values-openshift-scc.yaml \
  -f ./deploy/helm/openshell-dashboard/ci/values-route-edge.yaml \
  --set oidc.issuer=https://keycloak.apps.example.com/realms/openshell \
  --set openshiftRoute.host=dashboard.apps.example.com
```

The default `oidc.provider=oidc` works with any compatible OIDC issuer. Use `oidc.allowedGroups` for group restrictions supported by the provider. For Keycloak client/realm role checks, set `oidc.provider=keycloak-oidc` and `oidc.allowedRoles` (roles are alternatives). Other issuer-specific settings such as `oidc.scope` and `oidc.codeChallengeMethod` are optional; the generic OIDC scope defaults to `openid email profile`.

For Dashboard A, create the Secret outside Helm; do not put credentials or cookie keys in chart values or source control:

```sh
oc -n namespace-a create secret generic dashboard-a-oidc \
  --from-literal=client-id='openshell-dashboard-a' \
  --from-literal=client-secret='<DASHBOARD_A_CLIENT_SECRET>' \
  --from-literal=cookie-secret='<HIGH_ENTROPY_COOKIE_SECRET>'
```

Put only non-secret settings in a values file:

```yaml
gateway:
  url: grpcs://<gateway-service>.namespace-a.svc.cluster.local:<port>
  caSecretName: <gateway-ca-secret>
oidc:
  provider: keycloak-oidc
  issuer: https://keycloak.example.com/realms/openshell
  clientIdSecretKey: client-id
  existingSecret: dashboard-a-oidc
  adminRole: administrators-a
  allowedRoles:
    - openshell-api-a:users-a
    - openshell-api-a:administrators-a
  scope: openid profile email
  codeChallengeMethod: S256
authProxy:
  cookie:
    name: _openshell_a
    sameSite: lax
openshiftRoute:
  enabled: true
  host: dashboard-a.example.com
```

`oidc.clientIdSecretKey` reads the client ID from the same existing Secret and takes precedence over `oidc.clientId`. To use a non-Keycloak issuer, keep `oidc.provider=oidc` and omit `oidc.allowedRoles`. Edge Routes terminate TLS before oauth2-proxy; keep `authProxy.forceHTTPS=false` (default), with secure cookies enabled. Set `authProxy.forceHTTPS=true` only if proxy itself has HTTPS enabled via `authProxy.tls.secretName`.

Gateway TLS CA mounts `openshell-client-tls` key `ca.crt`, created by upstream certgen or cert-manager. Gateway URLs accept `grpcs://` or `https://` for TLS and `grpc://` or `http://` for plaintext. Only set `gateway.clientCertSecretName` if the gateway requires mTLS without OIDC. For `server.disableTls=true`, use `ci/values-tls-disabled.yaml` (no CA); browser ingress still needs HTTPS. The default dashboard image uses `quay.io/gkrumbach07/openshell-dashboard:<appVersion>`; the upstream oauth2-proxy image is pinned to `v7.9.0` until downstream image choice is settled. Override images by tag or immutable digest for releases.

The `keycloak`, `route-edge`, `route-reencrypt`, `gateway-api`, `mtls-client-cert`, `tls-disabled`, and `openshift-scc` overlays in `ci/` are renderable examples. Replace example hostnames, the reencrypt destination CA, and provision all referenced Secrets/ConfigMaps. For reencrypt, `authProxy.tls.secretName` supplies a proxy server certificate for the Route host; the Route validates it with `destinationCACertificate`. HTTPRoute forwards HTTP to proxy and needs a TLS-terminating Gateway for secure cookies. Preserve Host and WebSocket upgrade headers at any controller. The Route sets `timeout` and `timeout-tunnel` to 300s for terminal sessions.

NetworkPolicy allows ingress to the proxy port from `openshift-ingress` by default. When HTTPRoute is enabled, its Gateway namespace is selected instead. Override `networkPolicy.ingressNamespace` if the **data-plane proxy pods** live elsewhere; some ingress controllers use hostNetwork/node IPs and need cluster-specific policy configuration. Direct BFF access bypasses authentication; do not expose pod port 8080. Probe via exec on loopback. `gateway.preflight.enabled=true` checks an existing gateway Service on live Helm installations; keep it false for `helm template`.

Chart version and appVersion start at `0.0.0`; release CI stamps both with the released image version and publishes `oci://ghcr.io/gkrumbach07/openshell-dashboard/helm-chart/openshell-dashboard`. Stable OCI versions are never overwritten; installers pin chart version and image digest separately. CI also publishes a floating `0.0.0-dev` chart whose appVersion is the matching `sha-<commit>` image tag. For downstream registry mirrors, override `global.image.registry` and each component repository/digest.
